column21:
Balancing STEM and non-STEM courses can be tricky. One big challenge is managing time. STEM classes need lots of time for problem-solving, labs, and understanding theories, while non-STEM classes, like "Art of Living," focus more on thinking, discussion, and self-reflection. Handling both needs good planning.

Another challenge is the different ways of learning. STEM subjects are logical and numbers-based, while non-STEM subjects are more about ideas, creativity, and personal opinions. Adjusting to both styles and doing well in them can be hard.
column22:

Non-STEM courses, like "Art of Living," help develop soft skills such as communication, emotional understanding, critical thinking, and ethics. These are important for leadership, teamwork, and seeing the human side of science and technology.

A good education combines both STEM and non-STEM courses, helping students become skilled in technical areas while also understanding people and society, so they can solve problems with both logic and insight.

As a result, non-STEM courses are sometimes perceived as less relevant or less impactful in shaping future-ready professionals.
